notes: Source checks cover the listed claims, not every claim in the inherited handbook.
Local probes ran on CPython 3.12.14/Linux. Windows batch behavior, SQLAlchemy integration, pytest teardown, and Python 3.14/3.15 execution were not run.

claims.claim: A behavioral subtype must not require stronger preconditions or promise weaker postconditions; relevant invariants and history constraints still apply.

scope.topic: Behavioral subtyping; not merely static assignability

claims.review_trigger: Recheck when changing the canonical contract or subtype evaluation expectations.
claims.validation: Primary research inspected; contract is a design criterion, not an interpreter feature.

claims.claim: __iadd__ may return a different object or NotImplemented; the method does not guarantee in-place mutation.

scope.python: Documented Python 3.14 data model; reproduced on CPython 3.12.14

claims.review_trigger: Recheck when editing operator/protocol guidance.
claims.validation: Local probe confirmed fresh result and unchanged original object.

claims.claim: Defining __set__ or __delete__ makes a descriptor a data descriptor; overriding instance dictionary reads also requires __get__.

scope.python: Documented Python 3.14 data model; reproduced on CPython 3.12.14

claims.review_trigger: Recheck when changing attribute lookup guidance.
claims.validation: Local probes cover get+delete precedence and delete-without-get instance reads.

claims.claim: Decorator application occurs when the decorated definition executes; nested definitions can execute after import and repeatedly.
claims.review_trigger: Recheck when changing import-time or decorator guidance.
claims.validation: Local probe confirmed nested decorator invocation only when the enclosing call executes.

claims.claim: Ordinary imports reuse sys.modules entries; reload and other module identities can execute initialization again. Python 3.15 explicit lazy imports may defer initialization.

scope.python: Ordinary imports:3.14 docs/3.12.14 probe; explicit lazy imports:3.15 documentation

claims.review_trigger: Recheck when adding import-hook/lazy-import guidance or changing minimum Python.
claims.validation: Local ordinary-import/reload probes passed; 3.15 lazy import checked in docs only.

claims.claim: Awaiting an already-ready operation need not suspend; asyncio.sleep(0) supplies a cooperative checkpoint.
claims.review_trigger: Recheck if event-loop scheduling guidance or eager execution assumptions change.
claims.validation: 10,000 immediate awaits did not run a peer; sleep(0) then allowed it.

claims.claim: gather propagates the first exception without cancelling siblings; an outer timeout that already returned on error does not later clean them up, and cancelling a done gather does not cancel them.
claims.review_trigger: Recheck on asyncio API changes or changes to fallback/ownership cases.
claims.validation: Local early-error-before-timeout probe left sibling pending; explicit cancellation and join cleaned it up.

claims.claim: TaskGroup normally groups child failures; except* matches members, while ordinary except ExceptionGroup handles the group and propagation is valid.
claims.review_trigger: Recheck on TaskGroup exception-policy changes.
claims.validation: Ordinary except ExceptionGroup caught the grouped child failure in a local probe.

claims.claim: Structured task lifetime does not cap task count; a semaphore caps holders but not waiting tasks, so growing work needs an admission/pending-work policy.
claims.review_trigger: Recheck when changing queue/fan-out recommendations.
claims.validation: A local probe created 50 pending tasks behind a semaphore with one holder; all were joined.

claims.claim: A multi-statement operation confined to one loop thread need not lock when it cannot suspend, re-enter, or race outside thread access; thread-shared operations need their own ownership argument.

scope.python: Cooperative asyncio task interleaving; explicit assumptions exclude threads and reentrancy

claims.review_trigger: Recheck whenever concurrency domain or callback/reentrancy assumptions change.
claims.validation: Local 8-task confined counter probe preserved 800 updates; not a proof for arbitrary callbacks or threads.

claims.claim: Windows .bat/.cmd launch may invoke a system shell even with shell=False; native argv defaults and batch-file escaping require different analysis.

scope.platform: Windows batch launch; native executable argv recommendation separately scoped

claims.review_trigger: Recheck for subprocess security updates or a changed wrapper/executable.
claims.validation: Official caveat inspected. Linux native argument-data probe passed; Windows batch behavior not executed.

claims.claim: SQLAlchemy 2.0 noload can return unloaded None/empty state, while raiseload raises on unexpected access; raiseload does not prevent every unit-of-work flush load.
